 :Judgment:
This claim petition emanates in respect of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner by name Chethan Kumar in respect of the Road Traffic Accident dated 22.08.2014.

After disposal of this petition on 07.12.2016 MFA bearing No.2995/2017 was preferred before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka and as per the order in MFA No.2995/2017 dated 30.07.2025, the matter is remanded to this Tribunal for fesh consideration.

Succinctly stated the facts germane to the lis involved in this petition are briefly summarized as follows:
That on 22.08.2014 at about 7.30 p.m., when the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider in motorbike bearing Reg.No.KA-01-EH-4201 ridden by one Kumaraswamy and when they reached near Gollahalli main road, Tavarekere hobli,
Bengaluru South Taluk, at that time, rider of the motorbike bearing Reg.No.KA-01-EH-4201 (herein after referred to as the offending vehicle) drove in a rash and negligent manner with high speed, without observing any traffic rules and regulations and due to his negligence, lost control over the bike and came to his extreme left side and fell down, resulting in the accident.
It is submitted that the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries all over the body due to the impact of the accident.
3. Immediately, after the accident petitioner was shifted to Mathru hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.
Hence, the petitioner has claimed compensation of  SCCH 15 4 MVC No.2591/2015 Rs.8,00,000/- with cost and interest at the rate of 12% p.a in the interest of justice and equity.
4. In pursuance of service of notice issued to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed exparte.

Respondent No.2 filed Written Statement contending as follows:
The respondent No.2 denies that it has issued insurance policy to the offending vehicle in favour of the respondent No.1 and denied liability to indemnify the respondent No.1.
The Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied that the accident was caused by rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.
The rider of the motorcycle did not have valid and effective driving license.

The age,
avocation of the petitioner is denied.
The petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties.
Hence, on these grounds Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

SCCH 15 5 MVC No.2591/2015 5. Vide order dated 11.04.2016 the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :-
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries as mentioned in column No.11 in a road traffic accident on 22.08.2014 at about 7.30 p.m., on Gollahalli main road, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk, due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorbike bearing Reg.No.KA-01-EH-4201?
2)
Whether Petitioner is entitled for any compensation?

If so, to what extent and from whom?
3) What Order or Award?

6. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and examined two witnesses as PW.2 and 3 and relied upon Ex.P.1 to 15 SCCH 15 6 MVC No.2591/2015 documents and the Respondent No.2 has examined one witness as RW.2 and relied upon Ex.R4 and 5 documents.
7. Oral submissions were advanced by Ld. Counsel for parties in this case.

Having perused the records my issue wise findings run as under:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3 :

As per the Final Order  for the following :
 REASONS 8. Issue No.1: Before adjudication of the issue with respect to the compensation it is quintessential to adjudicate on the issue of negligence.
It is the contention of the petitioner that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorbike bearing Reg.No.KA-01-EH- Chetan Kumar vs Muthuraj .M

SCCH 15 7 MVC No.2591/2015 9.

In this regard the petitioner got himself examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination he has deposed that on 22.08.2014 at about 7.30 p.m. the petitioner was proceeding in motorbike bearing Reg.No.KA-01-EH-4201 as a pillion rider, which was driven by its rider by name Kumaraswamy on Gollahalli main road, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk, in a rash and negligent manner,
endangering human life, without observing any traffic rules and regulations and due to his negligence, he lost control and came to the extreme left and fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
10. The petitioner in support of his claim has in addition to describing the course of the accident in line with the facts mentioned in the complaint has relied upon Ex.P1 to 6 documents.
Ex.P1 is copy of the Complaint given by the petitioner and Ex.P2 is the FIR registered against the rider of the offending vehicle on the basis of the Complaint given by the petitioner on 26.08.2014.

Further Ex.P3 and ExP4 are the SCCH 15 8 MVC No.2591/2015 mahazars prepared at the spot of the accident at the time of the seizing motorbike and on perusal of Ex.P3 it discloses that the accident road is Tavarekere - Gollarahatti main road and towards left side footpath there were glass pieces indicating the spot of the accident and the width of the road is about 20 feet and at the left side there were brake marks of the bike found.

The fact of existence of the brake marks and the fact that accident has taken place without involvement of any other vehicles infers that the accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the rider of the motorbike and it infers that he lost control over the vehicle resulting in the accident.
Further, Ex.P5 is the wound certificate which discloses that the petitioner has sustained injuries due to the impact of the said accident.
Ex.P6 is the charge sheet filed against the rider of the motorbike for the offenses under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC and Sec.187 of IMV Act.

The said charge sheet also discloses that the motorist rode the motorbike in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and SCCH 15 9 MVC No.2591/2015 went to the extreme left side of the road and fell down from the bike resulting in the accident.
Hence, these documents satisfactorily establish the factum that the accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.

11. As far as the manner of the accident is concerned, PW.1 is cross-examined by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 and in the cross-examination of PW.1 he has deposed that the rider of the motorbike is his brother and he has given complaint in the police station and he took treatment at Mathrushree hospital as an inpatient.
He has denied that injuries sustained are not due to the accident but self fall and denied that his brother's motorbike is falsely implicated in this case to make wrongful gain.

Except the suggestion that the accident has taken place due to their own negligence nothing much is elicited in the cross-examination of PW.1 to disprove that the accident took place due to the negligence or rashness on the part of rider of the offending vehicle.
The petitioner has SCCH 15 10 MVC No.2591/2015 clearly and categorically deposed about the manner of the accident.
The oral testimony of PW.1 has stood unrebutted and PW1 has withstood the cross-examination of Respondent No.2.

There is no material on record which suggests falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW.1 as to the facts and circumstances surrounding cause of the Chetan Kumar vs Muthuraj .M on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150376732/
4 accident.

The fact that the rider of the offending vehicle has already been charge sheeted for the offenses under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC and Sec.187 of IMV act itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.
The certified copies of FIR, charge sheet, IMV report and Spot mahazar also corroborate the oral testimony of PW.1.
In view of medical records there is no dispute regarding the nature of injuries sustained by PW.1 in the above accident.
In view of the said discussion it is satisfactorily established that PW.1 suffered grievous injuries on account of rashness and negligence of rider riding the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
Hence, issue No.1 is answered in favour of the petitioner and in the 'Affirmative'.
SCCH 15 11 MVC No.2591/2015 12. Issue No.2:
In view of the findings on issue No.1 in favour of petitioner, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
The computation of compensation will have to be decided separately under various heads.
MEDICAL OR TREATMENT EXPENSES:

The petitioner has produced Ex.P5 - Wound certificate and also produced Ex.P7 - Discharge summary which discloses that the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient from 22.08.2014 to 27.08.2014 and he has sustained injury to his left leg.
In addition the petitioner has produced Ex.P8 - Medical bills and Ex.P9 Prescriptions.
The Petitioner has also produced case sheet of the hospital along with X-rays.
As far as the medical bills are concerned nothing much is elicited to disprove the authenticity of the said bills.
Hence petitioner is entitled to an amount of Rs.50,000/- under this head.
13. PAIN AND SUFFERING:

As per the medical documents the petitioner has sustained Type II compound comminuted fracture both bone (Tibia and Fibula) of left leg SCCH 15 12 MVC No.2591/2015 and it is stated in the petition that injuries sustained and physical impairment has caused unbearable pain and weakness in the left leg, difficulty to stand and bear weight on left leg,
to sit cross legged, squat on the floor, climb up and down staircase, to walk on the slope and walk on plain surface or do any work as prior to the accident.
It is not possible to ascertain quantum of compensation admissible to petitioner for the mental trauma, pain and sufferings etc., which he actually suffered due to the accidental injuries.

Keeping in view the trauma and nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Rs.30,000/- is awarded to him towards pain and sufferings.
Thus, he is awarded an amount of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
14. LOSS OF ACTUAL EARNINGS:
In his evidence PW.1 has submitted he was aged about 19 years and he was a painter and was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.

The medical records reflect that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries SCCH 15 13 MVC No.2591/2015 which has resulted in the disability and hence certainly he is unable to resume his work as prior to the accident.
It is submitted by the petitioner was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
In this regard, the petitioner has not produced any documents to show his income and avocation goes to show that there is no proof to establish the income and avocation of the petitioner.

In the absence of any material as to the monthly earnings of the Petitioner it would be proper to assume the monthly earnings of the petitioner as per the notional income which is taken as Rs.6,000/- p.m.

Taking into consideration Chetan Kumar vs Muthuraj .M on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150376732/
5 that the petitioner due to the injuries might not have been in a position to work for at least 2 months hence, as such the petitioner is entitled to an amount of Rs.6,000 X 2 = 12,000/- under this head.

sentences.text: 15. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS DUE TO DISABILITY:

The petitioner has claimed in his affidavit that he had sustained permanent disability to his left leg and in order to prove the same he got examined Orthopedic surgeon as PW.2 SCCH 15 14 MVC No.2591/2015 and PW.2 in his evidence deposed that the petitioner has sustained physical impairment and it is not progressive and not likely to improve in future and submitted that he assessed disability to whole body disability as 15%.

PW.2 is cross- examined by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 and PW.2 in his cross-examination admitted that he has not treated the petitioner and admitted that fracture of the petitioner is united and admitted that implants in-situ in tibia.
Nothing much is elicited in the cross-examination of PW.2 to disprove the disability assessed by PW.2.
The evidence of PW.2 discloses that the petitioner had sustained 15% disability to the whole body.
However said disability to the whole body appears to be on the higher side, it can be reduced to 10%.
The monthly income of the petitioner is already assessed at Rs.6,000/- at the relevant time.
As far as, age of the petitioner at the time of the accident is concerned on perusal of the petitioner's wound certificate Ex.P5 the age of the petitioner mentioned as 18 years.
Going by the same, the age of SCCH 15 15 MVC No.2591/2015 petitioner as on date of accident i.e., 22.08.2014 was around 18 years.

Therefore, in view of the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Corporation and another (2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the recent judgment dated 31.10.2017 given in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi &
Ors. SLP (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014, the multiplier of '18' is held applicable for calculating the loss of future earnings of petitioner arising out of his above disability.

The loss of future earnings of petitioner due to his above injury and permanent physical disability comes to Rs.1,29,600/-
(Rs.6,000/- X 12 X 18 X 10%) which can be rounded off Rs.1,30,000/- and the same is awarded to him as compensation under this head.
16. Loss of Amenities:

In view of the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, the extent of permanent physical SCCH 15 16 MVC No.2591/2015 disability and the extended period of medical treatment, the petitioner is granted a sum of Rs.10,000/- under this head.
17. Attendant's charges, Special diet and Conveyance:
The facts show that physical condition of the petitioner is such that he might have taken the help of an attendant.
Further, he would be requiring conveyance for movement.
His avocation has been hit due to his disablement.
He might have spent considerable amount towards special diet during his treatment.

Therefore, petitioner Chetan Kumar vs Muthuraj .M on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150376732/
6 is granted Rs.10,000/- under this head.

sentences.text: 18. COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
It is stated in the evidence of PW.2 that Petitioner needs another surgery for the removal of the implant from tibia.
But he has not produced estimation.
However, by considering the further surgery, it is proper to grant compensation of SCCH 15 17 MVC No.2591/2015 10,000/-.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,000/- under this head.

19. TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering  30,000/-
2. Loss of amenities  10,000/-
3. Loss of income during the laid  12,000/-
up period 4. Attendant's charges, Extra diet,  10,000/-
and conveyance 5.

Medical expenses  50,000/-
6. Loss of Future Income  1,30,000/-
7.

Future medical expenses  10,000/-
Total 2,52,000/-

20 . Regarding Liability: As far as the liability is concerned after disposal of the case on 07.12.2016 MFA was SCCH 15 18 MVC No.2591/2015 preferred bearing No.2995/2017 before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka and as per the order in MFA No.2995/2017 dated 30.07.2025, the matter is remanded to this Tribunal with the direction to cross-examine RW.2 and by giving liberty to insurance company to examine any other witnesses with an opportunity to cross-examine those witnesses and to dispose of the matter afresh, after hearing both sides on the issue of liability.
Hence after remand of the matter, the case has restored to its original number and respondent No.2 has filed additional written statement.
In addition, the official of respondent No.2 company is examined as RW.2 and filed affidavit in lieu of chief-examination and Ex.R4 and Ex.R5 are marked.

The counsel for the petitioner has fully cross- examined RW.2 and since there was no further evidence Chetan Kumar vs Muthuraj .M on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150376732/
7 on either side
, the matter was heard on merits on the question of liability.

Though the official of respondent No.2 company was examined as RW.1 however, the evidence of RW.1 was discarded since even though RW.1 was recalled for cross- SCCH 15 19 MVC No.2591/2015 examination however, subsequently RW.1 remained absent and did not tender for cross-examination.

Hence, after remand of the matter the present official who is Administrative Officer of respondent No.2 company is examined as RW.2 and in his evidence he has deposed that the respondent No.2 insurance company has issued Liability Only Policy in respect of the motorbike bearing Reg.No.KA-01-EH-4201 (offending vehicle) and the respondent No.2 has not collected any premium to cover the risk of pillion rider.
Hence, it is submitted by respondent No.2 that the insurance company is not liable to indemnify the owner of the vehicle and the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

21. In this regard, RW.2 has produced Ex.R5 which is copy of insurance policy which discloses that said policy is Liability Only Policy and it has covered basic 3rd party risk only and no additional premium is paid to cover the risk of the pillion rider.
RW.2 is cross-examined by the learned counsel for petitioner
and in the cross-examination RW.2 has deposed SCCH 15 20 MVC No.2591/2015 that Ex.R5 policy is renewed policy and no proposal form is obtained at the time of renewal.

It is admitted that as per the proposal form the policy is issued and hence it is the contention taken that the respondent company has not produced the proposal form to disclose who is covered under the policy.
It is also contended by the counsel for petitioner that seating capacity of the motorbike is two persons and hence pillion rider is also covered.

However, on perusal of Ex.R5 it is crystal clear that it is liability only policy and it is only basic 3rd party cover and no premium is collected to cover the risk of the pillion rider and pillion rider will not become a 3rd party since only occupants of the opposite vehicle will be 3 rd party.

Hence, Ex.R5 insurance policy clearly discloses that the risk of the petitioner was not covered under the policy as on the date of the accident and hence the respondent No.2 is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.1 and respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle will have to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner.
SCCH 15 21 MVC No.2591/2015 22.

sentences.text: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Sec.147(1) Motor Insurance - Act policy - pillion rider - liability of insurance company - death of pillion rider on motorcycle when motor cycle met with accident - Tribunal observed that policy covered the risk of pillion rider and fastened liability on insurance company - motor cycle was insured under two wheelers liability only policy covering risk of third party and personal accident to owner - rider - pillion rider is not a third party and no additional premium was paid to cover risk of pillion rider - whether motor cycle was insured under act policy and Tribunal erred in fastening liability on insurance company assuming that policy was a package policy - held: yes.

Having considered the principle of law laid down in the aforesaid cited cases it is clear that the policy issued to the insured vehicle by respondent No.2 is an Act policy and no specific premium is collected for the pillion rider or occupant of the motor cycle and hence the question of the liability of respondent No.2 insurance company does not arise.

The policy in the instant case obtained by the insured vehicle is a statutory policy and it is only beneficial to the 3 rd party and SCCH 15 25 MVC No.2591/2015 that benefit cannot be extended to the owner of the offending vehicle.
Pillion rider of the motor cycle cannot be considered as 3rd party.
Hence in view of the clear observations made in the decisions cited for the learned counsel for the respondent No.2, the question of liability of respondent No.2 does not arise.
Therefore, owner is liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 is "Partly in the Affirmative".
23. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent No.1 U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The claim petition filed by the petitioner against respondent No.2 is hereby dismissed.

The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of 2,52,000/- along with Chetan Kumar vs Muthuraj .M on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150376732/
10 interest at the rate of 9% per annum from SCCH 15 26 MVC No.2591/2015 the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E- payment and after proper identification.
The remaining 25% award amount shall be deposited as F.D. in the name of the Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of three years.

The Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/-
Draw Award accordingly.

The amount already deposited by the respondent No 2 is ordered to be refunded to respondent No 2.

opennyai_summary.issue:
SCCH 15 5 MVC No.2591/2015 5. Vide order dated 11.04.2016 the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :-
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries as mentioned in column No.11 in a road traffic accident on 22.08.2014 at about 7.30 p.m., on Gollahalli main road, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk, due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorbike bearing Reg.No.KA-01-EH-4201?
2)
Whether Petitioner is entitled for any compensation?
If so, to what extent and from whom?
3) What Order or Award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The fact of existence of the brake marks and the fact that accident has taken place without involvement of any other vehicles infers that the accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the rider of the motorbike and it infers that he lost control over the vehicle resulting in the accident.
There is no material on record which suggests falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW.1 as to the facts and circumstances surrounding cause of the Chetan Kumar vs Muthuraj .M on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150376732/
4 accident.
The fact that the rider of the offending vehicle has already been charge sheeted for the offenses under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC and Sec.187 of IMV act itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.
The certified copies of FIR, charge sheet, IMV report and Spot mahazar also corroborate the oral testimony of PW.1.
In view of medical records there is no dispute regarding the nature of injuries sustained by PW.1 in the above accident.
In view of the said discussion it is satisfactorily established that PW.1 suffered grievous injuries on account of rashness and negligence of rider riding the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
In view of the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, the extent of permanent physical SCCH 15 16 MVC No.2591/2015 disability and the extended period of medical treatment, the petitioner is granted a sum of Rs.10,000/- under this head.
Hence, it is submitted by respondent No.2 that the insurance company is not liable to indemnify the owner of the vehicle and the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Sec.147(1) Motor Insurance - Act policy - pillion rider - liability of insurance company - scooter met with accident due to its rash and negligent driving and pillion rider sustained injuries - Tribunal considering that Rs.16 collected under the head extra loading would cover the risk of pillion rider awarded compensation against the insurance company - amount collected under the head extra loading cannot be held as premium collected to cover the risk of pillion rider as it is an additional cost incorporated in a policy to cover losses - scooter was insured under act policy and risk of pillion rider is not covered under Act policy - whether insurance company is absolved from liability - Held:
2022 ACJ 688, between New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Vs Promila Devi and others,
wherein it has been observed as follows:
SCCH 15 23 MVC No.2591/2015 Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Sec.147(1) Motor Insurance - Act policy - private vehicle - passenger risk - liability of insurance company - death of an occupant of car when car met with accident due to its rash and negligent driving - whether risk of occupant of a private vehicle is covered under act policy - Held: no occupant of car and pillion rider on a two wheeler are covered only under comprehensive policy.
2023 ACJ 1098, between HDFC Ergo Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs Sharmilaben Gopalbhai Vasava and others, wherein it has been observed as follows:
Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Sec.147(1) Motor Insurance - Act policy - pillion rider - liability of insurance company - insurance company disputes its liability on the ground that offending motorcycle was insured under act policy and risk of injured - pillion rider is not covered - whether risk of pillion rider is not covered under act Chetan Kumar vs Muthuraj .M on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150376732/
9 policy and insurance company be exonerated from liability - Held Yes 2024 ACJ 1000, between New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Monaka Sahoo and others, wherein it has been observed as follows:
Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Sec.147(1) Motor Insurance - Act policy - pillion rider - liability of insurance company - whether risk of pillion rider on a two-wheeler is covered under act policy - held: No SCCH 15 24 MVC No.2591/2015 2024 ACJ 1143,
between Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs Mahadevappa and others, wherein it has been observed as follows:
Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Sec.147(1) Motor Insurance - Act policy - pillion rider - liability of insurance company - death of pillion rider on motorcycle when motor cycle met with accident - Tribunal observed that policy covered the risk of pillion rider and fastened liability on insurance company - motor cycle was insured under two wheelers liability only policy covering risk of third party and personal accident to owner - rider - pillion rider is not a third party and no additional premium was paid to cover risk of pillion rider - whether motor cycle was insured under act policy and Tribunal erred in fastening liability on insurance company assuming that policy was a package policy - held: yes.
The policy in the instant case obtained by the insured vehicle is a statutory policy and it is only beneficial to the 3 rd party and SCCH 15 25 MVC No.2591/2015 that benefit cannot be extended to the owner of the offending vehicle.
Pillion rider of the motor cycle cannot be considered as 3rd party.
Therefore, owner is liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.

23. Issue No.3:
In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent No.1 U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The claim petition filed by the petitioner against respondent No.2 is hereby dismissed.
The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of 2,52,000/- along with Chetan Kumar vs Muthuraj .M on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150376732/
10 interest at the rate of 9% per annum from SCCH 15 26 MVC No.2591/2015 the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E- payment and after proper identification.
The remaining 25% award amount shall be deposited as F.D. in the name of the Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of three years.
The Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/-
Draw Award accordingly.
